title: Reverse Only Letters
statement: Given a string `s`, return a new string in which the English letters (`a`-`z` and `A`-`Z`) appear in reverse order while every other character stays at exactly the index it had in `s`. Letters keep their case; only their positions among the letter slots are reversed.
constraints: Every character of s has an ASCII code from 33 to 122
notes:
## Intuition

Reversing a string swaps the first and last characters, then the next pair inward, and so on. Here the non-letters are fixed in place, so they simply do not take part in any swap: two pointers walk inward from both ends and pause only on letters. (A simpler two-pass idea collects the letters, then writes them back into the letter positions from last to first.)

## Approach

1. Copy `s` into an array `chars` so characters can be swapped.
2. Put `left` at the first index and `right` at the last.
3. While `left < right`: if `chars[left]` is not a letter, step `left` forward; else if `chars[right]` is not a letter, step `right` back.
4. Otherwise both are letters: swap them and move both pointers inward.
5. Join `chars` back into a string and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "ab-cd"`, `left = 0`, `right = 4`. Both `a` and `d` are letters, so swap: `"db-ca"`, then `left = 1`, `right = 3`. Both `b` and `c` are letters, so swap: `"dc-ba"`, then `left = 2`, `right = 2`. The pointers meet, so the answer is `"dc-ba"`; the `-` never moved.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each step moves at least one pointer inward.
- Space: O(n) for the character array (strings are immutable in JavaScript).

## Pitfalls

- Letters are only `a`-`z` and `A`-`Z`. Characters such as `[`, `_` and `` ` `` sit between the two letter ranges in ASCII, so a test like `c >= 'A' && c <= 'z'` wrongly treats them as letters.
- Move only one pointer when it sits on a non-letter; moving both would skip a letter on the other side.
- Digits count as non-letters and must stay where they are.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `chars` | the characters of `s`, swapped in place |
| `isLetter` | tells whether a character is an English letter |
| `left` | pointer moving forward from the start |
| `right` | pointer moving backward from the end |

narration.2: Strings cannot be changed in place, so work on an array of characters.
narration.3: Only a-z and A-Z count as letters; everything else stays put.
narration.4: left starts at the first character...
narration.6: Keep going until the two pointers meet or cross.
narration.7: A non-letter on the left never moves...
narration.9: Likewise a non-letter on the right...
narration.10: ...is stepped past from the other side.
narration.12: Both pointers sit on letters: swap them, as an ordinary reversal would.
narration.13: Move left inward past the letter just placed.
narration.17: Join the characters back into the answer string.
